module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 277

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/277](https://www.erdosproblems.com/277)
- [Ha79] Haight, J. A., Covering systems of congruences, a negative result. Mathematika (1979),
  53--61.
-/

@[expose] public section

open scoped ArithmeticFunction.sigma

namespace Erdos277

/--
Is it true that, for every $c$, there exists an $n$ such that $\sigma(n)>cn$ but there is no
covering system whose moduli all divide $n$?

This was answered affirmatively by Haight [Ha79].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/1268917deaaaa0d674f651287027baa26cea9920/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos277.lean#L1294"]
theorem erdos_277 :
   answer(True) ↔ ∀ c : ℝ, ∃ n : ℕ, (σ 1 n : ℝ) > c * n ∧
      ∀ (m : StrictCoveringSystem ℤ), ∃ i, (n : ℤ) ∉ m.moduli i  := by
  sorry

end Erdos277

reformulations.difference: The source's clause "there is no covering system whose moduli are all distinct divisors of n (which are > 1)" is written as `∀ (m : StrictCoveringSystem ℤ), ∃ i, (n : ℤ) ∉ m.moduli i`. Moduli are ideals of ℤ, and "distinct" and "> 1" come from the structure fields (`injective_moduli`, `ne_top`, `ne_bot`), not from the theorem text. The statement also quantifies over all real c and all n : ℕ, including 0, with no positivity condition.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every ideal of ℤ is span{d} with d = |generator| ∈ ℕ. The conditions ≠ ⊥ and ≠ ⊤ give d ≥ 2. Injective ideals means the d's are distinct. The coset {r} + span{d} is the class r mod d, and (n:ℤ) ∈ span{d} ↔ d ∣ n. So ∃ i, n ∉ moduli i says some modulus does not divide n. Quantifying over all m then says no distinct-moduli covering system (moduli > 1) has all moduli dividing n. Using a subset of the divisors or all of them makes no difference, since adding congruences keeps a covering. The value n = 0 is excluded automatically: σ 1 0 = 0 and 0 > c·0 is false. Negative or small c is harmless, because a witness for max(c, 1) also works for c. I proved in Lean, without sorry, `lean_clause_iff_source n`: (∀ m : StrictCoveringSystem ℤ, ∃ i, (n:ℤ) ∉ m.moduli i) ↔ ¬ ∃ k (a : Fin k → ℤ) (d : Fin k → ℕ), Injective d ∧ (∀ j, 1 < d j ∧ d j ∣ n) ∧ ∀ z, ∃ j, (d j:ℤ) ∣ z − a j. From it I proved `erdos_277_iff_source`: the full right-hand side ↔ ∀ c : ℝ, ∃ n > 0, σ(n) > c·n ∧ that elementary non-covering condition. Both depend only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

review.notes:
No misformalization and no status issue. Details:

(1) Statement: I checked every part against the source's wording. Quantifiers: ∀ c, ∃ n, and ∀ covering systems ∃ modulus not dividing n. The bound is strict (σ(n) > cn), matching the source. The covering notion (finite, distinct moduli, moduli > 1) matches the site and the FFKPY07 definition of 'covering' H. answer(True) matches 'solved in the affirmative' (Haight 1979).

(2) Lean experiments in /workspace/review:
- scratch2.lean builds a concrete StrictCoveringSystem ℤ ({0 mod 2, 0 mod 3, 1 mod 4, 5 mod 6, 7 mod 12}) and proves the clause fails for n = 12, so the clause is not vacuous. It also shows n = 1 handles c < 1 and n = 0 never passes the σ clause.
- scratch3.lean proves the equivalence with an elementary rendering of the source's statement.

(3) Status: `research solved` plus the `formal_proof using lean4` link agrees with the source (PROVED; database 'proved (Lean)'). I followed the PROOFS.md checklist. The link is pinned to a commit and points at line 1294, which is `theorem erdos_277`. That theorem is word-for-word the FC right-hand side. Its locally copied CoveringSystem/StrictCoveringSystem definitions match FC's in content; the only differences are `Set.univ` vs `@Set.univ R` and an extra instance attribute used for the proof. The file has no sorry or axiom declarations and compiles in this sandbox (Lean 4.33.1) with only standard axioms.

(4) Optional, not defects:
- The theorem docstring uses the September 2025 site wording ('whose moduli all divide n'). The page now reads 'whose moduli all distinct divisors of n (which are >1)'. The Lean already encodes distinct moduli > 1 through StrictCoveringSystem, so nothing changes mathematically; the docstring could be refreshed.
- The page also lists Erdős's follow-up from [Er80]: with f(x) = max over non-covering m < x of σ(m)/m, is f(x) = o(log log x)? The site records a negative answer via van Doorn's observation plus Hough's theorem. The file does not formalize this variant; that is an omission, not a misformalization.
- The [Ha79] citation omits volume 26; this is cosmetic.

(5) I did not read Haight's paper or Erdős's original texts ([Er77c], [Er80], [ErGr80] p.27 — an image-only scan — and [Er82e]) directly. The problem statement is consistently documented by erdosproblems.com and FFKPY07.
